plain.text: The LORD was gracious to Sarah as he had said. She became pregnant and bore Abraham a son in his old age, at the very time God had promised. Abraham named him Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. Abraham was a hundred years old. Sarah said, "God has brought me laughter, and everyone who hears will laugh with me. Who would have said that Sarah would nurse children?" When Isaac was weaned, Abraham held a great feast.

Sarah saw Ishmael, Hagar's son, mocking, and said to Abraham, "Get rid of that slave woman and her son." Abraham was very distressed, because Ishmael was his son. But God told him to listen to Sarah, because his offspring would be traced through Isaac, and he would make Ishmael into a nation too. Early next morning Abraham gave Hagar food and water and sent her away. When the water ran out in the desert, she put the boy under a bush and sat at a distance, sobbing, "I cannot watch the boy die." God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar: "Do not be afraid; God has heard the boy crying." God opened her eyes and she saw a well of water. God was with the boy as he grew up in the desert and became an archer.

Abimelech and his army commander came to Abraham: "God is with you in everything you do." They asked Abraham to swear to treat them kindly. Abraham agreed, but complained about a well Abimelech's servants had seized. They made a treaty at a place called Beersheba, and Abraham gave seven lambs as a witness that he had dug the well. Abraham planted a tamarisk tree there and called on the name of the LORD, the Eternal God.

summary.bigIdea: God keeps his promise and Isaac is born, bringing laughter, and God also cares for Hagar and Ishmael in the desert.
points: At last, Isaac is born, just as God promised.
Sarah says, "God has brought me laughter."
When Hagar and Ishmael are sent away, God hears the boy and provides water.
summary.reflection: God kept his promise at exactly the right time. Is there something you are still waiting for God about?
